data.name: BULLET SOUL INFINITE BURST
data.detailed_description:
Bullet Soul is back with a new recipe: Burst! The same aggressive, bullet-cancelling gameplay, flashy pyrotechnics and addictive action, but now with refined level design, more modes and more destruction! Shooting fans of all abilities, it's time to welcome back the true spirit of Japanese shooting games!

Gameplay
Infinite Burst takes the basics of Bullet Soul and adds two major enhancements: first, Burst Mode with it's overhauled level design, brand new coin-collecting mechanics and the eponymous Combination Burst system. Secondly, Loop, the bonus character, is now available across all modes. In addition, Normal and Caravan modes have been redesigned and rebalanced with new enemies and attack patterns and when Musou (or Infinite Burst) Mode is unlocked, you can rain down destruction with the titular Infinite Burst.

Music
The resident musical chefs, Kenji Ito and Kohta Takahashi return and this time they've brought Jake 'Virt' Kaufman to add his own blend of spice to their aural feast!

Story
Mecha-warl, an empire of evil, who would use their military might to conquer space itself.
This is the tale of the brave few who stood against their threat.

Zenichi, Yun, Sadahl and Loop begin their struggle to once more rid the galaxy of this threat.

Features:
  • 4 modes (+1 hidden) and a whole new style of play: Combination Burst
  • 4 different ships, with Loop playable across all modes
  • Normal Mode has been re-balanced for veterans of Bullet Soul
  • Practice and perfect your score stage by stage in Bancho Mode
  • Caravan Mode makes a return with new enemy patterns and a new music track
  • Resonator are back and Jake "Virt" Kaufman is on remix duty!
  • Leaderboards divided by mode & ship with friend filters
  • Includes tate/vertical screen mode with X/Y scaling and smoothing

data.short_description: Bullet Soul Infinite Burst is a vertically scrolling shooting game crossing old-school gameplay with a bullet hell twist. It adds numerous gameplay enhancements over its predecessor, Bullet Soul, not least of which is Burst Mode. The same aggressive, bullet-cancelling gameplay, now with more destruction, more coins and more tunes.

reviews.review:
[b]Infinite Burst[/b] came out on Xbox 360 about three years after the original [b]Bullet Soul[/b], but on Steam, they were published only a few months apart. Having bought them about a year apart, I wish I'd known better at the time: [b]Infinite Burst[/b] is [i]not[/i] a sequel, just a remix of the same game.

The gameplay is always centered on shooting down enemies to make their bullets disappear, but in the new main mode, Burst, they turn into collectible coins for scoring. If they reach the bottom of the screen, they bounce back up and are worth even more, making for some fun situations where you try to collect bounced coins while also managing enemy bullets.

The eponymous Burst replaces bombs: launched when a bar filled by destroying enemies reaches full capacity, it temporarily makes the ship's weapons hugely powerful. Most importantly, coins generated while the Burst is active can further prolong it. The voice clips of the characters as they collect them are [i]very[/i] annoying, though.
Rather than the ship being shot down by a single bullet, there is now a single life but with a shield capable of tanking a few hits. Upon continuing, the Burst is not recharged, which alone makes for more challenge than just having some bombs ready with the next life or credit.

The characters have been rebalanced a bit. Loop, now selectable in any mode, has been nerfed in power, while still being fairly powerful and perfect for less experienced players; Zenichi now feels much better to use, no longer being too weak compared to the others; Sadahl offers more of a challenge.

Much as I squinted, I couldn't find any significant improvements or differences in the graphics, save for the extremely flashy weapons under Burst - so flashy, in fact, that they risk covering too much of the screen - the renewed character portraits, and the coins: they stand out, which is good for visual clarity, but also clash a lot with the style of everything else. [i]Tate[/i] mode is still iffy. At least the music is great; I like these arrangements more than the original soundtrack.

The port is basically the same, with a lack of visual options, a resolution locked to 720p, and even the same issue after the end credits roll that I reported in the review of the original. At least it runs without crashes or other issues.

While it hardly innovates, and even feels lazy at times - still no selectable difficulty levels? - [b]Infinite Burst[/b] is still quite a decent shmup in its own right, and is the superior version by virtue of having Normal mode, a remix of the original, along with Burst mode. And simply finishing the game with all four characters (a simple task, given there are always infinite credits) unlocks Musou mode: weapons in an infinite Burst (oh!), and bombs on top of that. Good luck even dying there! Unless you really want to appreciate even the smallest differences or are a collector, the "first" version is pretty much redundant.

One last note about the illustrations that appear after the end credits, depending on the character used. They are nice, but Loop's is not just fanservicey, it's quite NSFW; not unwelcome by me, just very out of place compared to the others. Then again, the Japanese Xbox cover definitely took notice of her assets...

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows7/8.1/10
  • Processador: Core i3 of Sandy Bridge generation or better
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Intel HD Graphics Series (It needs 1GB memory allocation)
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 4 GB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: Sound Devices compartible Direct Sound
  • Notas adicionais: XBox 360 compatible game controller strongly recommended

Recomendados:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows7/8.1/10 (64bit ver)
  • Processador: Core i5 of Ivy Bridge generation or better
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: Geforce (VRAM 1GB or better)
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0
